clue.text: Boy's fruit stuck in the throat

definitions.text: Boy's fruit stuck in the throat

parts.note: Adam is a boy's name, here in the possessive
an apple is a common fruit

explanation.surface: A lad has bitten into some fruit and it has lodged in his throat.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines as well as builds: legend has it that the forbidden fruit stuck in the first man's throat, giving the lump its name.
explanation.definitionFit: The laryngeal prominence on a man's neck is popularly named after the first man and the forbidden fruit lodged there.

clue.text: Plans that are bibulous at first sight, about Indian city

annotationWithheld.why: Plans that are bibulous at first sight, about Indian city (8): AGRA sits inside DIAGRAMS, but no clue words give the outer DI...MS, and no copy of the clue could be found to explain 'bibulous at first sight'
annotationWithheld.clue: Plans that are bibulous at first sight, about Indian city

clue.text: Name of the chap who's defamed

definitions.text: Name of the chap who's defamed

parts.words: Name of the chap who's defamed
parts.note: plays on the saying that a disgraced man's name is dirt, so the word asked for is literally his 'name'

explanation.surface: Someone asks what the slandered man is called.
explanation.walkthrough: From the idiom 'his name is mud', said of someone who has lost his good reputation.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'his name is mud' describes a person in disgrace, so the dirt itself becomes the disgraced man's name.

clue.text: A hut that's leaning

parts.note: a tilt is an old word for a canvas covering, tent or booth

explanation.surface: Someone points out a ramshackle shed that tips to one side.
explanation.walkthrough: TILT here is the old noun for an awning or rough shelter, not the verb; together with A it gives the adverb 'tipped'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tipped at an angle, not upright, is said to be on a slant.

clue.text: Bird crossing over the road

explanation.surface: A bird flies across a road.
explanation.walkthrough: A PELICAN crossing is a British pedestrian crossing with lights the walker operates; the name comes from 'pedestrian light controlled'.
explanation.definitionFit: A large fish-eating waterbird with a throat pouch; also the British name for a push-button pedestrian crossing.

clue.text: Catch half the score, in French at first, and cheer!

indicators.note: places the French word at the front of the build, ahead of the other pieces

parts.note: the French word for in is en
to catch a remark is to hear it
a score is twenty, so half of it is ten

explanation.surface: A sports fan, half-catching the score in French, gives a cheer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' moves EN to the front, though the clue gives it last.
explanation.definitionFit: To cheer someone in the sense of giving them courage or hope, as a verb.

clue.text: Personal weapon provided by firm on the quiet

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
sh is the call for silence

explanation.surface: A company quietly supplies a private weapon to someone.
explanation.walkthrough: A COSH is a British word for a short heavy club or truncheon.
explanation.definitionFit: A short weighted club carried for hitting someone, a hand weapon for one user.

clue.text: Beautiful script, graphically fabricated

indicators.note: something fabricated is made up or constructed, so the letters of the neighbouring word are put together afresh

explanation.surface: A lovely hand that turns out to be a graphic forgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fabricated' rearranges the letters of 'graphically'.
explanation.definitionFit: The art of fine handwriting with elegant lettering, done with pen or brush.

clue.text: To pinch pennies, little money invested in stocks and shares

indicators.note: money invested in stocks is put inside them, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: scrip is a word for share certificates
m is a short form of money, as in a monetary abbreviation

explanation.surface: A thrifty person puts small sums into the stock market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invested in' puts M inside SCRIP.
explanation.definitionFit: To economise severely and save every coin, the same as skimping.

clue.text: Chap finds something boring, in a monkey

parts.note: a chap is a man
a drill is a tool that bores holes

explanation.surface: A man finds something tedious about a monkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' looks like 'dull' but means making a hole, so the tool is a DRILL.
explanation.definitionFit: A large West African primate related to baboons, with a brightly coloured face.

clue.text: Term for a girl or a boy

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a word that names a child of either sex.
explanation.walkthrough: Hilary term is the spring term at Oxford and some other British universities and law courts.
explanation.definitionFit: The spring session at Oxford University and the Inns of Court; also a first name given to both women and men.

clue.text: Alarm when drug is pulled out of the cargo

indicators.note: the drug is removed from the cargo word, so one letter goes missing

parts.note: freight is goods carried as cargo
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Customs raise the alarm when drugs are found hidden in a ship's cargo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulled out of' removes E (ecstasy) from FREIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudden fear or a scare, as a noun.

clue.text: Doctor agrees suffering must end; this is applied, in the theatre

definitions.text: this is applied, in the theatre

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters of the next word are altered

parts.note: suffering is pain

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A doctor agrees that a patient's agony has to stop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' is a verb rearranging AGREES; 'end' takes T from 'must'.
explanation.definitionFit: Stage make-up actors put on their faces before going in front of the audience.

clue.text: A march is organised — it inspires loyalty

indicators.note: to organise is to arrange, so the letters given are set in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone organises a march, which rallies supporters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' rearranges the letters of A MARCH IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Personal magnetism that draws followers and devotion.

clue.text: One's often acting in some part or other

indicators.note: the letters given are made other than they are, so rearranged

explanation.surface: An actor is always playing one role or another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'other' rearranges the letters of IN SOME PART OR; 'some part or other' looks like a set phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who mimics others, whose job is pretending to be people.

clue.text: Pots react badly to the watcher

indicators.note: badly done means poorly arranged, so the letters are shuffled into a new order

explanation.surface: Kitchen pots behave poorly in front of someone looking on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges the letters of POTS REACT.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who looks on at an event, as an onlooker.

clue.text: Girl may be sitting on top of the trifle

definitions.text: may be sitting on top of the trifle

explanation.surface: A girl perches on a dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: A trifle is a British layered dessert of sponge, fruit, custard and cream, often decorated with candied green stems.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name; also the plant whose candied green stems decorate desserts.

clue.text: Steed that might, when turned out, shy and pelt on?

indicators.note: turned out means rearranged, so the letters of the words given are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: A horse that might, once let out, shy and gallop off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when turned out' rearranges SHY AND PELT ON; 'turned out' also suggests putting a horse to grass.
explanation.definitionFit: A small hardy horse breed from the Scottish islands in the far north.

clue.text: Unsuitable choice of song for a wake

definitions.text: Unsuitable choice of song for a wake

parts.words: Unsuitable choice of song for a wake
parts.note: a wake is a vigil, but it also suggests waking up, and a song meant to send someone to sleep would be wrong for that

explanation.surface: Someone picks the wrong tune for a funeral gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wake' looks like the funeral vigil; read it as waking, and a bedtime song is the last thing wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: A gentle song sung to a child to send it to sleep, the opposite of waking.

clue.text: See the officer scowl and go red

parts.note: CO is short for commanding officer
to lour is to frown or scowl

explanation.surface: Look at the officer frown and blush.
explanation.walkthrough: LOUR (also spelt lower) means to look sullen or frown.
explanation.definitionFit: To blush or flush in the face, as a verb.

clue.text: Pilot has collapsed? Take him here

definitions.text: Pilot has collapsed? Take him here

indicators.note: letters that have collapsed have fallen apart and are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A pilot has keeled over, so someone says to rush him to care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collapsed' rearranges PILOT HAS, and the whole clue also says where such a patient goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Where the sick and injured are taken for medical treatment.

clue.text: Much trouble when you bring edible root back, at the border

indicators.note: bringing the root back means writing its word from end to start

parts.note: a yam is an edible tuber
a hem is the border of a piece of cloth

explanation.surface: A cook brings back a root vegetable and stitches a border, causing chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns YAM into MAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaos and disorder, a great deal of trouble.

clue.text: Planet's hot quagmire

parts.note: Mars is a planet; the 's is a link
h is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A planet is described as a hot bog.
explanation.walkthrough: H for hot is the tap abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A boggy, waterlogged stretch of land, the same as a swamp.

clue.text: Money to keep holding at home

indicators.note: the keep holds the home word inside it

parts.note: a keep is the stronghold of a castle, a fort
in means at home

explanation.surface: Someone saves cash to keep at home.
explanation.walkthrough: The FORINT is the currency of Hungary.
explanation.definitionFit: The forint is the Hungarian unit of currency.

clue.text: A sign for what's wrong then for what's right, they say? It's a puzzle!

indicators.note: flags that the pieces are spoken, so their sound gives the answer

parts.words: A sign for what's wrong then for what's right
parts.note: a cross marks a wrong answer and a tick a right one, so this is A, CROSS, TICK

explanation.surface: A teacher's marks, cross then tick, leave a pupil puzzled.
explanation.walkthrough: A CROSS-TICK said quickly sounds like the answer; it is a puzzle whose lines' initial letters spell a word.
explanation.definitionFit: A poem or puzzle in which the first letters of each line spell out a word.

clue.text: One slipper?

parts.note: not a soft shoe but something that slips or slides, as on snow

explanation.surface: Someone holds up a single slipper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slipper' is read as 'one that slides', a runner fixed under the boot on snow.
explanation.definitionFit: A long runner strapped to the foot for gliding over snow.

clue.text: Courage called for on icy roads

explanation.surface: Bravery is needed when the roads freeze.
explanation.walkthrough: Spread on icy roads, grit is sand or crushed stone that gives tyres a grip.
explanation.definitionFit: Grit is pluck and determination; it is also the sand or gravel scattered on frozen roads.

clue.text: In time, house of representatives leaders will be seen mingling with mythical characters

indicators.note: the letters mingle, so all are mixed into a new order
the leaders of the words are their first letters

explanation.surface: Leaders of a legislature are seen rubbing shoulders with legendary figures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders' takes H and R from 'house' and 'representatives'; 'mingling with' mixes them with the letters of MYTHICAL ('characters' meaning its letters).
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping a regular beat, as music or movement in step with tempo.
